o: Split nums into k contiguous chunks of equal length n/k and reverse each chunk in place. [1,2,4,3,5,6] with k=3 becomes [2,1,3,4,6,5]. Trivially a simulation problem.
k: Chunk size is n/k; reverse each block independently.
In-place reversal with two pointers avoids extra memory.

a.i: For each block start i = 0, sz, 2sz, ..., swap elements symmetric within the block.
s: For each block, reverse it with two pointers.
a.t: O(n) — every element swapped at most once

w: Trivial; the only care point is computing chunk size once and trusting the divisibility guarantee. Follow-up: reverse only every second chunk, or rotate chunks instead.
